title: Chamber of Commerce Invitation Letters & Business Visas for Türkiye
seoTitle: Turkish Business Visas & Chamber Invitation Letters (2026)
metaDescription: Practical 2026 guide to Turkish business visas, notarized company invitations, consular timelines, and IST passport control for visiting executives.
quickAnswer: Most EU, UK, US, and Gulf passport holders enter Türkiye visa-free for short commercial meetings, while several Asian, African, and Middle Eastern nationalities require a consular sticker visa backed by a notarized Turkish company invitation. Visa decisions rest solely with Turkish diplomatic missions, so build a four-to-six-week lead time before booking non-refundable executive flights.

body.text: Which nationalities need a formal Turkish business visa rather than visa-free entry?

Citizens of countries without a visa-exemption agreement or unconditional e-Visa eligibility—including India, Pakistan, Nigeria, Egypt, and many Sub-Saharan African and South Asian states—must apply for a consular sticker visa for commercial meetings. Travelers holding valid Schengen, UK, US, or Irish visas may qualify for a conditional e-Visa depending on nationality.

Always check the official [Republic of Türkiye Ministry of Foreign Affairs visa regime table](https://www.mfa.gov.tr/visa-information-for-foreigners.en.mfa) before scheduling board visits or factory audits. Under [MFA general visa rules](https://www.mfa.gov.tr/general-information-about-turkish-visas.en.mfa), passports generally must remain valid for at least 60 days beyond the permitted stay duration, and standard commercial entry covers meetings, negotiations, and trade fairs—never hands-on employment or paid local installation work, which requires a separate work permit.

body.text: What notarized invitation letter from a Turkish company is required?

Turkish consulates typically require an original invitation letter drafted on the inviting Turkish company’s letterhead, signed by an authorized signatory, and notarized by a Turkish notary public (Noter). The letter must state the invitee’s full passport details, exact travel dates, business purpose, and who covers accommodation and expenses during the stay.

According to [MFA general visa documentation rules](https://www.mfa.gov.tr/general-information-about-turkish-visas.en.mfa), the host company must also attach its current tax registration plate (vergi levhası), Trade Registry Gazette excerpt (Ticaret Sicil Gazetesi), and authorized signature circular (imza sirküleri). Where a delegation visits through an industry association or bilateral business council, a Chamber of Commerce (such as ITO or TOBB) endorsement strengthens the file, though the consulate holds final discretion over acceptable supporting papers.

items: Host company packet: Notarized invitation letter, tax plate, activity certificate (faaliyet belgesi), and signature circular.
Applicant packet: Employer dispatch letter on home-company letterhead, recent bank statements, travel medical insurance, and confirmed hotel reservations.
Alignment check: Ensure passport numbers, company names, and entry dates match character-for-character across the invitation, flight booking, and pre-application form.

body.text: How long does consular processing take?

Standard consular processing for a Turkish business sticker visa usually takes 10 to 20 business days after the in-person appointment, though security clearances referred to Ankara can extend approval to four or six weeks. Peak trade-fair months—particularly April, May, October, and November—regularly create multi-week appointment backlogs at busy missions.

Executives should initiate the [Turkish sticker visa pre-application](https://www.mfa.gov.tr/pre-application-system-for-turkish-sticker-visa.en.mfa) at least six weeks ahead of departure. Courier shipping of the wet-ink notarized invitation from Istanbul to the applicant’s home country adds three to five days on its own. Booking flexible hotel rates and changeable airline tickets prevents financial loss if a consulate requests an additional Chamber confirmation or supplementary corporate document.
What documents should executives carry at IST passport control?

Even with a valid visa or visa-free passport, border officers at Istanbul Airport (IST) can ask visiting executives to prove the commercial purpose and funding of their trip. Carry printed copies of your notarized invitation letter, return flight itinerary, confirmed hotel booking, and local host contact details in your cabin bag.

Review the [Istanbul Airport arrival passenger guide](https://www.istairport.com/en/flights/airport-guides/arrival-passenger-guide?locale=en) and [IST passport control points overview](https://www.istairport.com/en/flights/airport-guides/arrival-passenger-guide/services/complimentary-services/passport-control-points?locale=en) before landing, especially during evening wide-body arrival waves when standard queues lengthen. Keep commercial samples declared properly if carrying demonstration hardware, and never rely solely on phone screenshots when airport Wi-Fi or battery levels fail at the booth.

faq.q: Can a Turkish Chamber of Commerce issue an invitation letter directly to a foreign executive?
faq.a: Chambers of Commerce generally endorse trade delegations or verify a Turkish member company’s standing via an activity certificate, while the legally responsible invitation letter comes from the specific Turkish host company.

faq.q: Does a Turkish business visa allow me to install machinery or work on-site?
faq.a: No. Standard business visas cover meetings, factory inspections, negotiations, and trade shows. Hands-on technical installation, consulting delivery, or local employment requires a formal work permit or ministry exemption.

faq.q: Must the Turkish invitation letter be sent by physical courier?
faq.a: Many Turkish consulates still require the original wet-ink notarized invitation at the appointment, though some missions accept scanned copies for initial review. Always confirm with your local consulate before dispatching.

faq.q: Can an e-Visa be used for attending a trade fair in Istanbul?
faq.a: Yes, if your nationality qualifies for a Turkish e-Visa. Under MFA rules, e-Visas cover both tourism and short-term commercial visits, including trade fair attendance and supplier meetings.

faq.q: What happens if my passport has less than six months of validity?
faq.a: Türkiye applies a general rule requiring passport validity of at least 60 days beyond your visa or visa-free stay period, meaning a 90-day stay typically requires at least 150 days of remaining validity at entry.

faq.q: Can Itinerary of Türkiye guarantee my Turkish business visa approval?
faq.a: No. ITO is an independent logistics and advisory firm. Only Turkish embassies, consulates, and relevant government authorities adjudicate visa applications and border entry decisions.
